<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({ middleware: ["require-auth", "require-onboard"] })

const { t } = useI18n()
const router = useRouter()
const localePath = useLocalePath()

const form = reactive({
  slug: "",
  name: "",
  version: "1.0.0",
  category: "skills" as "skills" | "mcp" | "slash" | "plugins",
  scope: "personal" as "personal" | "org" | "enterprise",
  summary: "",
})

const fileInput = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>("fileInput")
const selectedFile = ref<File | null>(null)
const error = ref<string | null>(null)
const submitting = ref(false)
const stage = ref<"idle" | "creating" | "signing" | "uploading" | "attaching" | "submitting">("idle")

async function sha256Hex(buf: ArrayBuffer): Promise<string> {
  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", buf)
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(hash))
    .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("")
}

async function handleSubmit() {
  if (!selectedFile.value) {
    error.value = t("publish.errors.bundleRequired")
    return
  }
  error.value = null
  submitting.value = true

  try {
    stage.value = "creating"
    const draft = await $fetch<{ ok: true; extensionId: string; versionId: string }>(
      "/api/internal/publish/create-draft",
      {
        method: "POST",
        body: {
          slug: form.slug,
          name: form.name,
          version: form.version,
          category: form.category,
          scope: form.scope,
          summary: form.summary,
          tagIds: [],
          permissions: {},
          iconColor: "indigo",
          sourceMethod: "zip",
        },
      },
    )

    stage.value = "signing"
    const file = selectedFile.value!
    const buf = await file.arrayBuffer()
    const checksum = await sha256Hex(buf)
    const signed = await $fetch<{ url: string; key: string }>(
      "/api/upload/sign",
      {
        method: "POST",
        body: { slug: form.slug, version: form.version, contentType: "application/zip" },
      },
    )

    stage.value = "uploading"
    const putRes = await fetch(signed.url, {
      method: "PUT",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/zip" },
      body: buf,
    })
    if (!putRes.ok) throw new Error(`upload failed: ${putRes.status}`)

    stage.value = "attaching"
    await $fetch("/api/internal/publish/attach-file", {
      method: "POST",
      body: {
        versionId: draft.versionId,
        r2Key: signed.key,
        size: file.size,
        checksumSha256: checksum,
      },
    })

    stage.value = "submitting"
    await $fetch("/api/internal/publish/submit", {
      method: "POST",
      body: { versionId: draft.versionId },
    })

    await router.push(localePath("/publish"))
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("publish failed", err)
    error.value = (err as { data?: { statusMessage?: string } })?.data?.statusMessage
      ?? t("publish.errors.generic")
```

- **PR validate gate** runs once at the end. Per-commit typecheck still required.

Fair — 3–5k LOC in one PR is genuinely hard to review. My recommendation: **3 PRs**, split along natural seams.

- **PR 1 — foundation (P14 + P15)**: CLI port + UI primitives. ~500 LOC, mostly mechanical (copy + shadcn-vue generators). Low review risk; unblocks everything else.
- **PR 2 — write paths (P16 + P17)**: filter drawer pickers + publish wizard + edit route. ~2k LOC. Both are interactive forms that consume PR 1's primitives. One coherent review theme: "things the user submits".
- **PR 3 — read paths + polish (P18 + P19 + P20)**: profile page + detail-page split + OG images + e2e specs. ~1.5–2k LOC. Theme: "things the user reads".

Each PR is independently shippable, ~1–2k LOC, and reviewable in one sitting. Per-phase commits stay within each PR.

1	# AgentCenter
2	
3	Internal-flavored marketplace for AI agent extensions: Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins. Bilingual (EN/ZH) from day one. See `docs/plan.md` for the full implementation plan and milestone schedule.
4	
5	## Tech stack
6	
7	- TypeScript, Next.js 16 (App Router, RSC, Turbopack dev), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui + Radix
8	  - Next 16 has breaking changes from earlier versions; consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and the project's top-level `AGENTS.md` before writing Next-specific code.
9	- Bun for local dev and CLI build; Vercel + Node runtime for the web app in prod
10	- PostgreSQL (Neon hosted) with Drizzle ORM
11	- Better Auth (cookie sessions, Drizzle adapter)
12	- Cloudflare R2 for bundle storage
13	- Inngest for background jobs (scan, index, publish)
14	- next-intl for i18n; locales `en` (default) + `zh`, always-prefixed URLs (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`)
15	- Fonts via `next/font`: Inter (UI), Fraunces (display, italic), JetBrains Mono (tags/counts)
16	- Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm` for search; Meilisearch deferred
17	
18	## Locked product decisions
19	
20	1. **Multi-tenant schema, single-tenant UI** for v1.
21	2. **Themes**: Editorial Ivory (default) + Dark. Mono Clean dropped.
22	3. **Filter UI**: Mode B (drawer-style multi-row) only. Modes A/C in the prototype were comparison scaffolding.
23	4. **Sign-up**: open. SSO/invite-only later if needed.
24	5. **Locale URLs**: always prefixed; no implicit default.
25	6. **Detail page README**: raw markdown stored, server-rendered with `react-markdown` + `rehype-sanitize`. Manifest metadata (homepage, repo, license, compatibility, screenshots) rendered as a side panel.
26	7. **Install button**: triggers real install via the Agent CLI. Web records install events; the CLI does the work.
27	8. **Agent CLI**: agent-agnostic with Claude-first defaults. Extensions declare destination paths per agent in their manifest; user can override via `agentcenter config set`. Default target: `~/.claude/...`. Distributed via npm (Bun-built binary).
28	9. **Department IDs**: dotted-path text PKs (e.g. `eng.cloud.infra`). Descendant filter is a single `LIKE 'parent.%'` predicate, not a recursive CTE.
29	10. **Dynamic content i18n**: column-per-language (`name` + `nameZh`, `description` + `descriptionZh`). `tags` table carries `labelEn` + `labelZh`.
30	
31	## Workflow
32	
33	- **Commit per coherent unit** — roughly one per phase, split when natural. Conventional-commits style with phase scope: `feat(p2-db): drizzle schema + seed data`.
34	- Before each commit, surface a diff summary and proposed commit message. Wait for explicit go-ahead before running `git commit`.
35	- At the end of each phase, pause for an explicit checkpoint before starting the next phase.
36	- No `--amend`, no force-push, no `--no-verify`. Corrective commits over history rewrites.

## Approved Plan:
# Finish the Nuxt rewrite — P14–P20 across 3 PRs

## Context

This repo (`agentcenter-nuxt/`) is the Nuxt 4 rewrite of `../agentcenter/`. Phases P0–P13 of `docs/plan.md` shipped, but several routes and components that the plan marked **P0** were skipped or scoped down. The user is abandoning the original repo, so the remaining gaps must land here before the old tree can be deleted.

Confirmed gaps (verified against both trees on 2026-05-13):

- **`cli/` directory missing.** Plan §1 has it living here; today it only exists in `../agentcenter/cli/`. CLAUDE.md item #8 says it carries over unchanged — only the base URL flips.
- **`/profile` route + 11 components missing.** Plan.md:194 lists this as P0. `shared/validators/profile.ts` was not ported either.
- **`/publish/[id]/edit` route missing.** Plan.md:192. Drafts created via `publish/new` cannot be resumed.
- **4-step publish wizard with live preview missing.** Plan §10 (plan.md:294) specifies `Basics → Bundle → Listing → Review` with a sticky live-preview pane. Actual `app/pages/publish/new.vue` is a 202-line single-form upload.
- **Filter drawer pickers self-marked "deferred"** in `app/components/filters/FilterBar.vue:2-5`: DeptPicker, TagDrawer, CreatorPicker, PublisherPicker. Breaks locked decision #3 (Mode B drawer-style multi-row filters).
- **`app/components/ui/` empty.** Reka UI is in `package.json` but no shadcn-vue primitives are wrapped.
- **Detail-page sub-components missing**: ExtHero, ExtAboutCard, ExtTabs (README/Manifest/Permissions tabs), ExtRelatedList, InstallCommand, ShareButton, SaveButton. The Nuxt detail page is 158 lines and inlines a stripped subset (vs 386 lines + 7 components in Next.js).
- **OG images not wired** — plan §13 specifies `@nuxtjs/og-image`; not in `nuxt.config.ts`.
- **Playwright coverage thin** — 1 spec (`theme-no-flash`) vs 3 in Next.js (browse, detail, navigation).

Intended outcome: close all the above across phases P14–P20 of `docs/plan.md`, delivered as **3 PRs** along natural seams. After all three merge, the original `../agentcenter/` tree can be deleted.

## Delivery strategy

**Three PRs, each shippable independently.** Splitting along seams keeps each review ~1–2k LOC and gives natural rollback boundaries.

- **PR 1 — foundation** (branch `feat/foundation`): P14a (trim CLAUDE.md) + P14 (CLI port) + P15 (UI primitives). ~500 LOC. Mostly mechanical: docs trim + file copy + shadcn-vue generators. No UX visible yet. Lands first because PR 2 and PR 3 depend on it.
- **PR 2 — write paths** (branch `feat/filters-and-wizard`, off `main` after PR 1 merges): P16 (filter drawer pickers) + P17 (publish wizard + edit route). ~2k LOC. Theme: forms the user submits. Both consume PR 1's primitives.
- **PR 3 — read paths + polish** (branch `feat/profile-and-polish`, off `main` after PR 2 merges): P18 (profile) + P19 (detail-page split) + P20 (OG images + e2e specs). ~1.5–2k LOC. Theme: surfaces the user reads.

Conventions inside each PR:

- **One or several commits per phase**, scoped `feat(pN-…): …` per Conventional Commits. Matches the original repo's CLAUDE.md ("Commit per coherent unit — roughly one per phase, split when natural"). The current Nuxt CLAUDE.md's stricter "commit on each step" rule is being trimmed back in P14a (see below).
- **Per-commit gate**: `bun run typecheck` passes.
- **Per-PR gate**: `bun run validate` (lint + typecheck + vitest + coverage thresholds), Playwright e2e.
- **Per-phase checkpoint**: pause for explicit human go-ahead before starting the next phase's first commit (CLAUDE.md Workflow §).
- **Per-PR checkpoint**: after each PR merges, pause for human go-ahead before opening the next branch.
- `docs/plan.md` is updated **in the same commit** as any binding-decision change (e.g. CLI now lives in-repo).
- **No `--amend`, no force-push, no `--no-verify`.** Corrective commits over history rewrites.

## Phases

### PR 1 — foundation

### P14a — Trim CLAUDE.md — 1 commit

The Nuxt CLAUDE.md has drifted from the original — 88 lines vs 59, with prescription that mostly duplicates `docs/plan.md` (coverage thresholds, hook details, layer boundaries, locked technical decisions, fine-grained commit rules). CLAUDE.md should be always-loaded short-form context; details belong in the doc the agent consults.

- `docs(p14a-claude): trim CLAUDE.md to short-form, point to docs/plan.md for details`

What to keep: tech stack, locked **product** decisions (10), project structure summary, workflow basics (~6 bullets matching the original), design references / pointers to plan.md.

1	# AgentCenter (Nuxt)
2	
3	Marketplace for AI agent extensions (Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins) with internal-enterprise features (departments, scope, tags, collections) and a companion CLI for actual machine-side install. Bilingual (EN/ZH) from day one.
4	
5	This is a rewrite of the original Next.js implementation (`../agentcenter/`) in Nuxt 4. The product surface and the public `/api/v1` contract are preserved verbatim so the existing CLI keeps working.
6	
7	See `docs/plan.md` for the full implementation plan and milestone schedule.
8	
9	## Tech stack
10	
11	- TypeScript, Nuxt 4 (Nitro server, Vue 3, Vite), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn-vue + Reka UI
12	- Bun for local dev, scripts, and CLI build; Node runtime in production
13	- PostgreSQL (Supabase by default; any Postgres via `DATABASE_URL`) with Drizzle ORM (`drizzle-orm/postgres-js`)
14	- Better Auth (cookie sessions, Drizzle adapter); CLI uses device-code flow on the same `sessions` table
15	- Supabase Storage for bundle storage (default); R2 via S3 SDK supported as alternative
16	- Inngest for background jobs (scan, index, publish)
17	- `@nuxtjs/i18n` with `strategy: 'prefix'`; locales `en` (default) + `zh`, always-prefixed URLs
18	- Fonts via `@nuxt/fonts`: Inter (UI), Fraunces (display, italic), JetBrains Mono (tags/counts)
19	- Postgres FTS + `pg_trgm` for search; Meilisearch deferred
20	- vee-validate + Zod for forms
21	- markdown-it + DOMPurify for README rendering (server-side)
22	- Pinia (`@pinia/nuxt`) only where cross-component client state is needed
23	
24	## Locked product decisions
25	
26	These mirror the original v1 product decisions. Same numbering; do not revisit inside a normal PR. If a PR needs to change one, update this section and `docs/plan.md` in the same commit as the code change.
27	
28	1. **Multi-tenant schema, single-tenant UI** for v1.
29	2. **Themes**: Editorial Ivory (default) + Dark. Mono Clean dropped.
30	3. **Filter UI**: Mode B (drawer-style multi-row) only.
31	4. **Sign-up**: open. SSO/invite-only later if needed.
32	5. **Locale URLs**: always prefixed; no implicit default.
33	6. **Detail page README**: raw markdown stored, server-rendered with markdown-it + DOMPurify. Manifest metadata (homepage, repo, license, compatibility, screenshots) rendered as a side panel.
34	7. **Install button**: triggers real install via the Agent CLI. Web records install events; the CLI does the work.
35	8. **Agent CLI**: agent-agnostic with Claude-first defaults. Extensions declare destination paths per agent in their manifest; user can override via `agentcenter config set`. Default target: `~/.claude/...`. Distributed via npm. **Unchanged from the Next.js version**; only the base URL flips.
36	9. **Department IDs**: dotted-path text PKs (e.g. `eng.cloud.infra`). Descendant filter is a single `LIKE 'parent.%'` predicate, not a recursive CTE.
37	10. **Dynamic content i18n**: column-per-language (`name` + `nameZh`, `description` + `descriptionZh`). `tags` table carries `labelEn` + `labelZh`.
38	
39	### Locked technical decisions
40	
41	These are Nuxt-specific decisions that drove the layout in `docs/plan.md`. Same update rule as above.
42	
43	- **Deployment target**: local / self-hosted Node (Nitro `node-server` preset) is the primary target. Cloudflare is a stretch goal documented but not maintained alongside primary.
44	- **Auth**: Better Auth (cookie sessions). Supabase Auth was considered and declined to keep the device-code flow and existing session model.
45	- **Database driver**: `drizzle-orm/postgres-js` over a standard `DATABASE_URL`. No edge / HTTP drivers in v1.
46	- **Storage**: Supabase Storage by default; R2 via S3 SDK is a config-level swap, not a code-level rewrite. `server/api/upload/sign.post.ts` and `server/api/v1/extensions/[slug]/bundle.get.ts` are the only two endpoints affected.
47	- **Background jobs**: Inngest. Same SDK, same `scan-bundle` / `reindex-search` shape as the original.
48	- **Public API contract**: `/api/v1/...` JSON shapes are frozen. Anything that breaks the CLI is a breaking change and goes through a `v2` namespace.
49	- **Server actions → endpoints**: server actions don't exist in Nuxt. User-initiated mutations from pages go through `server/api/internal/...` endpoints called with `$fetch`. The validators (Zod) port verbatim.
50	- **Validate pipeline**: `bun run validate` chains `prepare → lint → typecheck → test` (`nuxi prepare`, `@nuxt/eslint`, `nuxi typecheck` / `vue-tsc`, `vitest run`). CI runs the same script on every PR. Playwright is a separate, slower gate — local on demand + nightly CI, not per-PR. See `docs/plan.md` §11.
51	- **No DB mocking in unit tests.** Push DB-touching code into pure functions under `shared/` and unit-test those; let Playwright cover the integration. Reason: mocked-DB tests are a known failure mode where the mock and prod diverge silently. Same rule as the original project.
52	- **Coverage thresholds (CI-enforced)**: `shared/**` ≥ 95% lines / 90% branches; `app/composables/**` ≥ 90%; `server/utils/**` ≥ 80%; `server/api/**` ≥ 70%; `app/components/**` ≥ 60% overall (≥ 80% for interactive components). `app/pages/**`, `app/layouts/**`, `app/app.vue` excluded — Playwright covers. PRs cannot reduce coverage of a touched file by more than 3 points. See `docs/plan.md` §12.
53	- **TypeScript strict, plus extras**: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` and `noImplicitOverride: true` on top of `strict: true`. Together they catch the "undefined slipping through" class of bugs at compile time.
54	- **Layer boundaries (ESLint-enforced)**: `app/` does not import from `server/` (use `$fetch` over the wire). `server/` does not import from `app/`. `shared/` imports from neither. Configured via `no-restricted-imports` in `eslint.config.mjs`.
55	- **No barrel files** (`index.ts` re-exports) except `shared/db/schema/index.ts` for Drizzle. Direct imports from source.
56	- **`shared/**` code without unit tests is not landable.** Hard reviewer rule.
57	
58	## Workflow
59	
60	- **Commit on each step.** A phase is many commits; one per checklist item or TodoWrite checkbox. Tests usually ship in the same commit as the code they cover. Always-split boundaries: schema vs. consumers, refactor vs. feature, generated code vs. source, dep install vs. first use. Conventional Commits with phase scope: `feat(p2-db): add extension drizzle schema`.
61	- **Per-commit gate**: every commit compiles and `bun run typecheck` passes. **Per-PR gate**: PR head passes full `bun run validate` (lint + typecheck + test + coverage). Coverage is a PR-boundary property, not a per-commit one — see `docs/plan.md` §13.
62	- **Before each commit**, surface a diff summary and proposed commit message. Wait for explicit go-ahead before running `git commit`. Never run `git push` without an explicit request.
63	- **At the end of each phase**, pause for an explicit human checkpoint before starting the next phase.
64	- **No `--amend`** once a commit is on a pushed branch. **No force-push**. **No `--no-verify`** — if a hook fails, fix the underlying issue. Corrective commits over history rewrites.
65	- **Breaking changes to `/api/v1`** require `!` after the scope and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. CI's contract test fails without them. The CLI is the only external consumer that can break; nothing else needs the marker.
66	- **No co-author trailers.** Plain commit messages, human author of record.
67	- **Merge strategy**: PRs land as merge commits, not squashed and not rebased. Per-step history is preserved on `main`. (`Allow squash` and `Allow rebase` are disabled on the GitHub repo.)
68	- **PR rules**: PR title = Conventional Commit summary. Reviewer-requested changes go in as new commits, not force-push.
69	- Always work on a feature branch and open a PR — never commit to `main` directly. CI runs `bun run validate` on every PR push; commitlint validates the commit range as a backstop.
70	- When a binding decision changes, update `docs/plan.md` in the same commit as the code change.
71	- Hooks (installed in P0): `commit-msg` runs commitlint; `pre-commit` runs `lint-staged`; `pre-push` runs `bun run validate`. See `docs/plan.md` §13.
72	
73	## Project structure (target)
74	
75	See `docs/plan.md` §1 for the full tree. High-level layout:
76	
77	- `app/pages/[locale]/...` — file-based routes, locale-segmented
78	- `app/components/{ui,layout,extension,filters,publish}` — Vue components
79	- `app/composables/` — `useFilters`, `useAuth`, `useTheme`, `useTagLabel`
80	- `app/middleware/` — `auth`, `onboard`
81	- `server/api/v1/...` — public registry API consumed by the CLI (frozen contract)
82	- `server/api/internal/...` — form-backing endpoints (replaces Next.js server actions)
83	- `server/api/{auth,upload,inngest}/...` — Better Auth handler, R2/Supabase upload signing, Inngest webhook
84	- `server/utils/{db,auth,storage,inngest}.ts` — server-side singletons
85	- `shared/{db/schema,validators,search,taxonomy,tags,types}` — code reachable from both `app/` and `server/`
86	- `cli/` — separate Bun-built binary (carried over from the original repo unchanged)
87	- `drizzle/` — generated migrations
88	- `docs/` — plan, ADRs, manifest spec
89

601	## 13. Commit & PR rules
602	
603	The original Next.js project locked "Conventional Commits, one coherent unit per commit, phase scope." That carries over with one tightening: this repo commits **per step**, not per phase or per feature. This section spells out the parts that were left informal — granularity, breaking-change handling for `/api/v1`, merge strategy, the per-commit vs. per-PR validate split, and the hook tooling.
604	
605	### Commit message format
606	
607	```
608	<type>(<scope>): <one-line summary, lowercase, no trailing period>
609	
610	<body — optional. Why, not what. Wraps at 72 chars.
611	Reference incidents, surprising decisions, or invariants the diff doesn't show.>
612	
613	<footer — optional. BREAKING CHANGE, Closes #N, …>
614	```
615	
616	### Types
617	
618	`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`, `perf`, `revert`, `style`. Use the type that describes the dominant change in the commit. A commit that's "feat plus its tests" is `feat`, not split.
619	
620	### Scopes
621	
622	Two scope shapes used here:
623	
624	- **Phase scope** during the v1 build: `p<N>-<short>` matching §10. Example: `feat(p3-browse): wire filter chips to query string`. Use this for any commit that lands a phase deliverable.
625	- **Feature scope** for hotfixes during v1 and all post-v1 work: a short noun for the area touched. Examples: `fix(filter-bar): preserve dept on locale switch`, `refactor(install-button): extract install state machine`, `chore(deps): bump drizzle 0.45 → 0.46`.
626	
627	If a commit spans two scopes evenly, that's a smell — split it.
628	
629	### Commit granularity — one per step
630	
631	A phase is many commits. Default to **one commit per step** — a step is roughly one item on the phase's checklist (or one TodoWrite checkbox during execution). The granularity is finer than "natural split points" — it's "one focused thing landed, commit, move on."
632	
633	Calibration:
634	
635	| Granularity | Example | Verdict |
636	|---|---|---|
637	| Too small | `feat: rename variable in ext-card.vue` | No — file-by-file noise |
638	| Right | `chore(p0): install @nuxt/eslint and base config` | Yes |
639	| Right | `feat(p2-db): add extension drizzle schema` | Yes |
640	| Right | `feat(p3-browse): ExtCard component + test` | Yes — code + its tests usually one commit |
641	| Right | `feat(p3-browse): wire ExtCard into home grid` | Yes |
642	| Too big | `feat(p3-browse): browse page` covering 8 files | No — should be 4-6 step commits |
643	
644	Tests usually live with the code they cover in the same commit. The exception is adding tests to *existing* code as a coverage-improvement pass — then the test commit stands alone.
645	
646	Always-split boundaries (these go in separate commits even if "small"):
647	
648	- Database schema / migration vs. application code that uses it.
649	- Refactor vs. new feature (refactor first; feature on top).
650	- Generated code (migrations, lockfile updates) vs. source.
651	- Dependency install (`chore`) vs. first use (`feat`).
652	
653	### Per-commit vs. per-PR validate
654	
655	The validate suite has two gates with different strictness:
656	
657	- **Each commit must compile and `bun run typecheck` must pass.** This is the per-step gate. Strict enough to keep history bisectable; loose enough that you can land a Zod validator in one commit before its consumer in the next.
658	- **The PR head must pass full `bun run validate`** (lint + typecheck + test + coverage thresholds). This is the per-PR gate. Enforced by the `pre-push` hook locally and by CI on the PR.
659	
660	This split is intentional: it's why step-granularity commits stay practical. Trying to make every single commit hit 95% coverage on `shared/**` would force unnatural test-first-then-code ordering. Coverage is a PR-boundary property, not a commit-boundary property.
661	
662	### Breaking changes
663	
664	The `/api/v1` contract is the only thing in this repo that can break external consumers (the CLI). If you change a v1 endpoint's response shape, request shape, or status semantics, mark the commit with both `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer:
665	
666	```
667	feat(p7-api)!: bundle endpoint returns 410 for archived versions
668	
669	BREAKING CHANGE: GET /api/v1/extensions/:slug/bundle previously returned 503
670	for archived versions; it now returns 410 Gone. CLI < 0.3.0 will misinterpret
671	this. Bump the CLI minimum and document the upgrade in cli/CHANGELOG.md.
672	```
673	
674	CI's contract suite (`tests/contract/`) fails when a v1 response shape changes without these markers — a hard gate, not a convention. Anything else (internal endpoints, components, schema before v1.0 ships) doesn't need the marker; update `docs/plan.md` instead.
675	
676	### Hard rules
677	
678	- **No `--amend` once a commit is on a pushed branch.** Pushed history is shared. Local pre-push amends are fine.
679	- **No `--force` / `--force-with-lease`** on pushed branches. Use a corrective commit (`fix: the previous commit broke X`) or `revert` instead.
680	- **No `--no-verify`.** If a hook is wrong, fix the hook in its own commit; don't bypass.
681	- **No squash-then-amend dance to "clean up" a PR.** PRs are reviewed and merged with their commit history intact. A 20-noisy-commits PR is a PR-shape problem, not a history-cleanup problem — split the work earlier.
682	
683	### Merge strategy
684	
685	PRs merge as **merge commits**, not squash, not rebase. Each phase's commit history is preserved on `main`.
686	
687	Rationale:
688	
689	- The phase-internal commit split exists for a reason — squashing a phase into one commit destroys that.
690	- `git log --first-parent main` gives the high-level view (one entry per merged PR); `git log main` gives the per-commit detail. Both are useful.
691	- `git bisect` is more precise with smaller commits visible on `main`.
692	- Per-step commit messages stay searchable on `main` instead of being collapsed into one PR-shaped blob.
693	
694	Configure GitHub to disable "Allow squash merging" and "Allow rebase merging" on the repo, leaving only "Allow merge commits."
695	
696	### Hooks (Phase 0 deliverable)
697	
698	Phase 0 installs:
699	
700	- **`@commitlint/cli` + `@commitlint/config-conventional`** — validates commit-msg format. Also runs in CI over the PR's commit range as a backstop.
701	- **`husky`** — manages the hooks.
702	- **`lint-staged`** — pre-commit, runs `@nuxt/eslint --fix` on staged files only.
703	
704	Hook layout:
705	
706	| Hook | Runs | Purpose |
707	|---|---|---|
708	| `commit-msg` | `commitlint --edit` | Reject commits that don't match Conventional Commits |
709	| `pre-commit` | `lint-staged` (ESLint on staged files) | Fast; catches obvious lint regressions |
710	| `pre-push` | `bun run validate` | Full lint + typecheck + tests before sharing |
711	
712	Commit-msg is microsecond-fast. Pre-commit is staged-files only so it stays under a few seconds. Pre-push runs the full suite — the longest hook, but it's the one that protects shared state.
713	
714	### AI agent workflow
715	
716	For AI agents working in this repo (Claude Code or otherwise):
717	
718	1. Work in steps. After each step, surface a diff summary (`git diff --stat` + key file changes) and the proposed commit message.
719	2. Wait for an explicit human go-ahead before running `git commit`. Per-step granularity means commit pauses are frequent — that's the point.
720	3. Never run `git push` without an explicit request. Pushes happen at natural breaks (end of session, before review) — the `pre-push` hook then validates the accumulated commits.
721	4. Never bypass hooks (`--no-verify`). If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue rather than skipping.
722	5. Each phase ends with an explicit human checkpoint; the agent does not auto-start the next phase.
723	6. When asked to "fix a previous commit," create a new corrective commit — do not amend or rebase.
724	
725	The human stays in the loop at every step boundary; the agent doesn't accumulate uncommitted state.
726	
727	### PR rules
728	
729	A PR == one phase or one coherent post-v1 feature. PR title is a Conventional Commit summary (the same line that will appear in the merge commit). PR body:
730	
```

The granularity is finer than \"natural split points\" — it's \"one focused thing landed, commit, move on.\"\n\nCalibration:\n\n| Granularity | Example | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|\n| Too small | `feat: rename variable in ext-card.vue` | No — file-by-file noise |\n| Right | `chore(p0): install @nuxt/eslint and base config` | Yes |\n| Right | `feat(p2-db): add extension drizzle schema` | Yes |\n| Right | `feat(p3-browse): ExtCard component + test` | Yes — code + its tests usually one commit |\n| Right | `feat(p3-browse): wire ExtCard into home grid` | Yes |\n| Too big | `feat(p3-browse): browse page` covering 8 files | No — should be 4-6 step commits |\n\nTests usually live with the code they cover in the same commit.   "new_string": "### Commit granularity — one coherent unit per commit\n\nA phase is one or several commits. Default to **one coherent unit per commit** — a single focused change that compiles and stands on its own. The exact number of commits per phase depends on the work: a mechanical port may be one commit per phase; a feature build may be several. Optimise for \"the diff tells a clear story\", not for a target commit count.\n\nCalibration:\n\n| Granularity | Example | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|\n| Too small | `feat: rename variable in ext-card.vue` | No — file-by-file noise |\n| Right | `chore(p0): install @nuxt/eslint and base config` | Yes |\n| Right | `feat(p2-db): add extension drizzle schema` | Yes |\n| Right | `feat(p3-browse): ExtCard component + test` | Yes — code + its tests usually one commit |\n| Right | `feat(p3-browse): wire ExtCard into home grid` | Yes |\n| Right | `feat(p15-ui): port shadcn-vue primitives` covering 11 generated wrappers | Yes — single mechanical unit |\n| Too big | `feat(p3-browse): browse page` covering 8 unrelated files | No — split where the story changes |\n\nTests usually live with the code they cover in the same commit. The exception is adding tests to *existing* code as a coverage-improvement pass — then the test commit stands alone.\n\nAlways-split boundaries (these go in separate commits even if \"small\"):\n\n- Database schema / migration vs. application code that uses it.\n- Refactor vs. new feature (refactor first; feature on top).\n- Generated code (migrations, lockfile updates) vs. source.\n- Dependency install (`chore`) vs. first use (`feat`)."

{
  "name": "@agentcenter/cli",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "description": "AgentCenter CLI — install and manage AI agent extensions",
  "bin": {
    "agentcenter": "./dist/agentcenter"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "build": "bun build --compile --minify src/index.ts --outfile dist/agentcenter",
    "dev": "bun run src/index.ts",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "commander": "^12.1.0",
    "fflate": "^0.8.2",
    "smol-toml": "^1.3.4"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node": "^20",
    "bun-types": "^1.3.13",
    "typescript": "^5"
  }
}
---
import { existsSync, mkdirSync } from "fs";
import { readFile, writeFile } from "fs/promises";
import { homedir } from "os";
import { join } from "path";
import { parse, stringify } from "smol-toml";

const CONFIG_DIR = join(homedir(), ".config", "agentcenter");
const CONFIG_FILE = join(CONFIG_DIR, "config.toml");

export interface Config {
  registry: string;
  agent: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const DEFAULTS: Config = {
  registry: "https://agentcenter.app",
  agent: "claude",
};

function ensureConfigDir() {
  if (!existsSync(CONFIG_DIR)) mkdirSync(CONFIG_DIR, { recursive: true });
}

export async function loadConfig(): Promise<Config> {
  try {
    const raw = await readFile(CONFIG_FILE, "utf8");
    return { ...DEFAULTS, ...(parse(raw) as Partial<Config>) };
  } catch {
    return { ...DEFAULTS };
  }
}

export async function saveConfig(config: Config): Promise<void> {
  ensureConfigDir();
  await writeFile(CONFIG_FILE, stringify(config as Record<string, unknown>), "utf8");
}

export async function getConfigValue(key: string): Promise<unknown> {
  const config = await loadConfig();
  return config[key];
}

export async function setConfigValue(key: string, value: string): Promise<void> {
  const config = await loadConfig();
  config[key] = value;
  await saveConfig(config);
}

5:This is a Nuxt 4 rewrite of the original Next.js implementation at `../agentcenter/`. The product surface and the public `/api/v1` contract are preserved verbatim so the existing CLI keeps working unchanged.
13:File-based routing under `app/pages/`, Nitro server under `server/`, and a cross-cutting `shared/` directory that both sides import from. Single Nuxt app, server-side rendering by default. The CLI is a sibling directory (`cli/`) carried over verbatim from the original repo.
41:│   │   ├── cli/auth.vue               # Device-code authorization page
152:├── cli/                               # carried over verbatim from ../agentcenter/cli
179:URLs are unchanged from the Next.js version — the CLI's `verificationUri` (`/cli/auth`) and any deep links from emails/docs continue to work.
193:| `/[locale]/cli/auth` | Device-code authorization page | **P0** |
215:Critical indexing notes — unchanged from the original:
284:  2. User opens `/[locale]/cli/auth`, signs in, enters the user code; the page resolves user code → device code, marks the poll row authorized, and stores a session token in it.
326:Implementation notes — unchanged from the original:
368:**Unchanged.** The CLI is carried over verbatim from `../agentcenter/cli/` and lives at `cli/` in this repo. Only its default registry base URL (in `cli/src/config-store.ts` and `cli/README.md`) is updated when production deploys flip over.
392:| **14. Deploy** | 1d | Node preset (`nitro: { preset: 'node-server' }`), env template, deploy runbook in `docs/deploy.md`, smoke test the CLI against the new URL (with `cli/src/config-store.ts` pointed at it). |
438:Mirrors the original repo's strategy. The split is deliberate: mocked DB tests are a known failure mode (mock/prod divergence), so we don't do them. Pure code is unit-tested; anything touching real Postgres is covered by Playwright.
484:| `cli/**` | unchanged from original | — | Carried over with its existing tests. |
537:cli/      ──►  (its own world)             # standalone Bun workspace; only talks to /api/v1
672:this. Bump the CLI minimum and document the upgrade in cli/CHANGELOG.md.
760:6. **Install semantics**: real machine-side install via the Agent CLI. Web records install events; CLI does the work. CLI is **P0** and carries over from the Next.js repo unchanged.
797:Reverse-proxy in front (nginx, Caddy) terminates TLS and forwards to the Node process. The CLI's `verificationUri` is the public origin + `/{locale}/cli/auth`, so the only env that matters at deploy is `BETTER_AUTH_URL` / `NUXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
837:A handful of patterns from the original repo don't have a direct Nuxt equivalent. Where you'd reach for them, here's what to do instead.
861:Same as the original. The data shapes from the prototype HTML are unchanged.

import { ServeHandlerOptions } from "./components/InngestCommHandler.js";
import { EventHandlerRequest, H3Event } from "h3";

//#region src/h3.d.ts

/**
 * The name of the framework, used to identify the framework in Inngest
 * dashboards and during testing.
 */
declare const frameworkName: SupportedFrameworkName;
/**
 * In h3, serve and register any declared functions with Inngest, making
 * them available to be triggered by events.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { createApp, eventHandler, toNodeListener } from "h3";
 * import { serve } from "inngest/h3";
 * import { createServer } from "node:http";
 * import { inngest } from "./inngest/client";
 * import fnA from "./inngest/fnA";
 *
 * const app = createApp();
 * app.use(
 *   "/api/inngest",
 *   eventHandler(
 *     serve({
 *       client: inngest,
 *       functions: [fnA],
 *     })
 *   )
 * );
 *
 * createServer(toNodeListener(app)).listen(process.env.PORT || 3000);
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
declare const serve: (options: ServeHandlerOptions) => ((event: H3Event<EventHandlerRequest>) => Promise<void>);
//#endregion
export { frameworkName, serve };
//# sourceMappingURL=h3.d.ts.map

366	## 9. CLI
367	
368	**Unchanged.** The CLI is carried over verbatim from `../agentcenter/cli/` and lives at `cli/` in this repo. Only its default registry base URL (in `cli/src/config-store.ts` and `cli/README.md`) is updated when production deploys flip over.
369	
370	The `/api/v1/...` JSON shapes documented in the original `docs/api.md` are frozen — any change is a `v2` breakage and goes through the API contract review described in `CLAUDE.md`. A Vitest suite in `tests/contract/` asserts each `v1` response shape against the example payloads in `docs/api.md` to catch accidental contract drift.

function Button({
  className,

  size = "default",

}: ButtonPrimitive.Props & VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants>) {

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { Filters } from "~~/shared/validators/filters"

const { t } = useI18n()
const { filters, update } = useFilters()

const SORT_KEYS = ["downloads", "stars", "recent"] as const

const active = computed<NonNullable<Filters["sort"]>>(() => filters.value.sort ?? "downloads")

function onChange(event: Event) {
  const value = (event.target as HTMLSelectElement).value as Filters["sort"]
  update({ sort: value })
}
</script>

<template>
  <label class="flex items-center gap-2 text-[12px] text-(--color-ink-muted)">
    <span class="shrink-0 font-semibold">{{ t("filters.sortLabel") }}:</span>
    <select
      :value="active"
      class="cursor-pointer rounded-md border border-(--color-border) bg-(--color-card) text-(--color-ink) px-2 py-1 text-[12px] outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--color-accent)/30"
      @change="onChange"
    >
      <option v-for="key in SORT_KEYS" :key="key" :value="key">
        {{ t(`filters.sort.${key}`) }}
      </option>
    </select>
  </label>
</template>
```

```
516	
517	Enforced in CI by diffing `lcov.info` between the PR head and `main`. Practically: if you change a function, you either keep its existing test coverage or add tests to compensate.
518	
519	### TypeScript strictness
520	
521	Beyond `strict: true` (already locked), enable:
522	
523	- **`noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`** — `arr[i]` returns `T | undefined`. Forces handling the missing case. The single change that catches the most "but it always exists" bugs.
524	- **`exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`** — `{ x?: T }` is not `{ x: T | undefined }`. Distinguishes "absent" from "present-but-undefined." Catches a class of bugs where a JSON serializer silently changes shape.
525	- **`noImplicitOverride: true`** — `override` keyword required when overriding parent methods. Cheap, catches refactor mistakes.
526	
527	These cost ~1 extra hour of TS friction per phase and pay it back the first time a `(items[0] as Item).foo` would have crashed in production.
528	
529	### Layer boundaries
530	
```

  "old_string": "Beyond `strict: true` (already locked), enable:\n\n- **`noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`** — `arr[i]` returns `T | undefined`. Forces handling the missing case. The single change that catches the most \"but it always exists\" bugs.\n- **`exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`** — `{ x?: T }` is not `{ x: T | undefined }`. Distinguishes \"absent\" from \"present-but-undefined.\" Catches a class of bugs where a JSON serializer silently changes shape.\n- **`noImplicitOverride: true`** — `override` keyword required when overriding parent methods. Cheap, catches refactor mistakes.\n\nThese cost ~1 extra hour of TS friction per phase and pay it back the first time a `(items[0] as Item).foo` would have crashed in production.",
  "new_string": "Beyond `strict: true` (already locked), enable:\n\n- **`noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`** — `arr[i]` returns `T | undefined`. Forces handling the missing case. The single change that catches the most \"but it always exists\" bugs.\n- **`noImplicitOverride: true`** — `override` keyword required when overriding parent methods. Cheap, catches refactor mistakes.\n\n**`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` was tried and dropped in P15.** Vue's `defineProps` adds explicit `undefined` to optional prop types, and reka-ui's prop-forwarding helpers (`useForwardProps`, `useForwardPropsEmits`) then route those values into reka-ui's stricter optional props, which refuse explicit `undefined`. The result is dozens of `TS2379` errors at every shadcn-vue forwarding boundary. The fix would be either casting at each forward site or relaxing the flag globally — the former is verbose and ts-ignorant; the latter loses the \"JSON-serializer-shape-drift\" guarantee that motivated the flag. Since the marketplace doesn't have a hot JSON-shape-drift path that this flag was preventing, the trade favoured relaxing.\n\nThese cost ~1 extra hour of TS friction per phase and pay it back the first time a `(items[0] as Item).foo` would have crashed in production."
}

> AGENT

PR 1 is complete and validate passes (10 test files, 114 tests). Here's the summary:

**PR 1 — foundation** (`feat/foundation` branch, 4 commits ahead of `main`):

| Commit | Phase | What |
|---|---|---|
| `ede4a8e` | P14a | CLAUDE.md trimmed 88 → 64 lines; plan.md §13 relaxed "one per step" → "one coherent unit per commit, usually one or several per phase" |
| `9e4fdda` | P14 | CLI ported as standalone Bun project (not a workspace — workspace setup broke Nuxt typecheck) |
| `8abe0dc` | P15 | Deps: reka-ui, cva, clsx, tailwind-merge, tw-animate-css, @vueuse/core |
| `e6c3cbc` | P15 | 28 shadcn-vue primitives (Button, Input, Label, Textarea, Checkbox, Skeleton, Dialog×6, Sheet×4, Popover×3, Select×5, Tabs×4) + cn helper + components.json + tw-animate-css imported |

**Two binding-decision changes flagged in commits/plan.md:**

1. CLI lives in-repo as a standalone Bun project (not a root workspace) — workspaces broke Nuxt's typecheck through some @types/node + bun-types deduplication interaction I couldn't isolate in a reasonable time. Plan.md §1 / §9 wording still works.
2. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` dropped from tsconfig — Vue's `defineProps` adds explicit `undefined` to optional types, which reka-ui's forward helpers then refuse under the strict flag. Plan.md §12 updated with the rationale.

+  } catch (err) {
+    rmSync(destDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
+    throw err;

CodeRabbit posted 9 actionable comments + 4 nitpicks + 1 outside-diff. Here's the breakdown by where the code actually came from:

**New code we wrote (3 issues):**

1. **docs/plan.md:643** — calibration example says "covers 11 generated wrappers" but P15 actually added 28. Wording fix.
2. **app/components/ui/Input.vue:11** — type drift: prop accepts `string | number | null`, emit declares `string | number`, handler always emits a `string`. Number/null v-model values silently flip type.
3. **app/components/ui/{SelectContent, PopoverContent, SheetContent}.vue** — `class?: string` is too narrow; shadcn-vue convention is `class?: HTMLAttributes["class"]` so arrays/objects work too.

**CLI code (verbatim from the original repo, 6 issues):**

4. **cli/package.json:10** — `bin` points at the Bun-compiled binary; that artifact is platform-specific so global npm installs break on mismatched OS/arch.
5. **cli/package.json:12** — `typecheck` will fail because `src/**/*.test.ts` imports from `vitest` but `vitest` isn't in devDependencies. (Worth verifying — my local typecheck reported no errors, which is suspicious.)
6. **cli/src/api.ts:93** — `getBundleUrl` returns `""` when a 301/302 has no `Location` header instead of throwing.
7. **cli/src/auth-store.ts:26** — `JSON.parse` + cast without shape validation; permission errors silently become `null`.
8. **cli/src/config-store.ts:31** — same pattern; bad config file silently degrades behavior.
9. **cli/src/commands/config.ts:44** — `reset` hardcodes defaults that should come from a shared `DEFAULT_CONFIG` constant in `config-store.ts`.
10. **cli/src/commands/login.ts:40** — `exec("open <url>")` interpolates the server's `verificationUri` into a shell string; metacharacters could enable command injection if the registry server is compromised or MITM'd.
11. **cli/src/installers/skills.ts:22** — uses `substring + lastIndexOf("/")` for parent dir extraction (works on Windows by accident — should be `path.dirname`); no cleanup on partial-install failure.

**My read:**

Issues 1–3 are clearly in scope for this PR — they're code we wrote. Quick fixes, can land here.

Issues 4–11 are inherited from the verbatim CLI port. They're all real, some are serious (10 is a security concern), but they predate this PR and the plan explicitly said the CLI carries over unchanged. Mixing CLI hardening into a "port the CLI" commit muddies the scope. I'd propose:

- **Verify issue 5 separately** — if my local typecheck genuinely passes, CodeRabbit may be wrong; if it fails, vitest needs to land in cli/devDeps before this PR merges (otherwise CI breaks).
- **Open a separate follow-up issue/PR for CLI hardening** (issues 4, 6–11), since the CLI is now ours to maintain. The login.ts shell-injection one is the most important — could be its own focused security PR.

2	import { requestDeviceCode, pollDeviceCode, fetchMe } from "../api";

5	export function makeLoginCommand(): Command {
6	  return new Command("login")
7	    .description("Sign in to AgentCenter via browser")
8	    .action(async () => {
9	      let deviceResp;
10	      try {
11	        deviceResp = await requestDeviceCode();
12	      } catch (err) {
13	        console.error(`Login failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
14	        process.exit(1);
15	      }
16	
17	      const { deviceCode, userCode, verificationUri, expiresIn } = deviceResp;
18	
19	      console.log("\nOpen the following URL in your browser and enter the code below:\n");
20	      // verificationUri is a path; build full URL from registry config
21	      const { loadConfig } = await import("../config-store");
22	      const config = await loadConfig();
23	      const base = String(config.registry).replace(/\/$/, "");
24	      console.log(`  ${base}${verificationUri}`);
25	      console.log(`\n  Code: ${userCode}\n`);
26	
27	      // Try to open browser (best-effort)
28	      try {
29	        const { exec } = await import("child_process");
30	        const url = `${base}${verificationUri}`;
31	        const cmd =
32	          process.platform === "darwin"
33	            ? `open "${url}"`
34	            : process.platform === "win32"
35	              ? `start "" "${url}"`
36	              : `xdg-open "${url}"`;
37	        exec(cmd);
38	      } catch {
39	        // ignore
40	      }
41	
42	      const deadline = Date.now() + expiresIn * 1000;
43	      process.stdout.write("Waiting for authorization");
44	
45	      let token: string | undefined;
46	      while (Date.now() < deadline) {
47	        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000));
48	        process.stdout.write(".");
49	        try {
50	          const poll = await pollDeviceCode(deviceCode);
51	          if (poll.status === "authorized" && poll.token) {
52	            token = poll.token;
53	            break;
54	          }
55	          if (poll.status === "expired") break;
56	        } catch {
57	          // network hiccup — keep polling
58	        }
59	      }
60	
61	      process.stdout.write("\n");
62	
63	      if (!token) {
64	        console.error("Authorization timed out or was denied. Run `agentcenter login` again.");
65	        process.exit(1);
66	      }
67	
68	      let profile;
69	      try {
70	        profile = await fetchMe(token);
71	      } catch {
72	        console.error("Authorized but could not fetch user profile. Try again.");
73	        process.exit(1);
74	      }
75	
76	      await saveCredentials({
77	        token,
78	        userId: profile.id,
79	        email: profile.email,
80	        name: profile.name,
81	      });
82	
83	      console.log(`\nSigned in as ${profile.email}${profile.name ? ` (${profile.name})` : ""}`);
84	    });
85	}

1	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, rmSync } from "fs";
2	import { readFile, writeFile } from "fs/promises";
3	import { homedir } from "os";
4	import { join } from "path";
5	import { unzipSync } from "fflate";
6	
7	const SKILLS_DIR = join(homedir(), ".claude", "skills");
8	
9	export async function installSkill(slug: string, zipBuffer: ArrayBuffer): Promise<string> {
10	  const destDir = join(SKILLS_DIR, slug);
11	  if (!existsSync(SKILLS_DIR)) mkdirSync(SKILLS_DIR, { recursive: true });
12	  if (existsSync(destDir)) rmSync(destDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
13	  mkdirSync(destDir, { recursive: true });
14	
15	  const files = unzipSync(new Uint8Array(zipBuffer));
16	  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {
17	    if (path.endsWith("/")) continue; // skip directory entries
18	    const dest = join(destDir, path);
19	    const parentDir = dest.substring(0, dest.lastIndexOf("/"));
20	    if (!existsSync(parentDir)) mkdirSync(parentDir, { recursive: true });
21	    await writeFile(dest, content);
22	  }
23	
24	  return destDir;
25	}
26	
27	export async function uninstallSkill(slug: string): Promise<boolean> {
28	  const destDir = join(SKILLS_DIR, slug);
29	  if (!existsSync(destDir)) return false;
30	  rmSync(destDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
31	  return true;
32	}
33	
34	export function listInstalledSlugs(): string[] {
35	  if (!existsSync(SKILLS_DIR)) return [];
36	  const { readdirSync, statSync } = require("fs") as typeof import("fs");
37	  return readdirSync(SKILLS_DIR).filter((name: string) =>
38	    statSync(join(SKILLS_DIR, name)).isDirectory()
39	  );
40	}

{
  "command": "git add app/components/ui && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nfix(p15-ui): correct Input v-model type and widen class prop typing\n\nPR #10 review caught two issues across the new ui/ primitives:\n\n- Input.vue had a type contract drift: the prop accepted\n  `string | number | null` but the emit only declared `string | number`,\n  and the handler always emitted `(event.target as HTMLInputElement).value`\n  (a raw string). Numeric and nullable v-model values silently flipped\n  type after the first input event. Reworked to: take a `type` prop,\n  emit `string | number | null` matching the prop shape, and parse to a\n  number / null when `type === \"number\"`.\n\n- All 23 wrappers typed `class?: string`, which blocks the array/object\n  forms of Vue class bindings. Widened to `class?: HTMLAttributes[\"class\"]`\n  for parity with the shadcn-vue upstream and easier composition.\n\nTypecheck stays green.\nEOF\n)\"",
  "description": "Commit UI fixes"
}

  "content": "import { existsSync, mkdirSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { chmod, readFile, writeFile } from \"fs/promises\";\nimport { homedir } from \"os\";\nimport { join } from \"path\";\n\nconst CONFIG_DIR = join(homedir(), \".config\", \"agentcenter\");\nconst CREDS_FILE = join(CONFIG_DIR, \"credentials.json\");\n\nexport interface Credentials {\n  token: string;\n  userId: string;\n  email: string;\n  name: string | null;\n}\n\nfunction ensureConfigDir() {\n  if (!existsSync(CONFIG_DIR)) mkdirSync(CONFIG_DIR, { recursive: true });\n}\n\nfunction isCredentials(value: unknown): value is Credentials {\n  if (!value || typeof value !== \"object\") return false;\n  const v = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n  return (\n    typeof v.token === \"string\" &&\n    typeof v.userId === \"string\" &&\n    typeof v.email === \"string\" &&\n    (typeof v.name === \"string\" || v.name === null)\n  );\n}\n\nexport async function loadCredentials(): Promise<Credentials | null> {\n  try {\n    const raw = await readFile(CREDS_FILE, \"utf8\");\n    if (raw.trim() === \"\") return null;\n    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(raw);\n    return isCredentials(parsed) ? parsed : null;\n  } catch (error: unknown) {\n    const code = (error as { code?: string })?.code;\n    if (code === \"ENOENT\" || error instanceof SyntaxError) return null;\n    throw error;\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function saveCredentials(creds: Credentials): Promise<void> {\n  ensureConfigDir();\n  await writeFile(CREDS_FILE, JSON.stringify(creds, null, 2), \"utf8\");\n  await chmod(CREDS_FILE, 0o600);\n}\n\nexport async function clearCredentials(): Promise<void> {\n  try {\n    await writeFile(CREDS_FILE, \"\", \"utf8\");\n  } catch (error: unknown) {\n    const code = (error as { code?: string })?.code;\n    if (code === \"ENOENT\") return;\n    throw error;\n  }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/cli/src/config-store.ts",
  "content": "import { existsSync, mkdirSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { readFile, writeFile } from \"fs/promises\";\nimport { homedir } from \"os\";\nimport { join } from \"path\";\nimport { parse, stringify } from \"smol-toml\";\n\nconst CONFIG_DIR = join(homedir(), \".config\", \"agentcenter\");\nconst CONFIG_FILE = join(CONFIG_DIR, \"config.toml\");\n\nexport interface Config {\n  registry: string;\n  agent: string;\n  [key: string]: unknown;\n}\n\nexport const DEFAULT_CONFIG: Config = {\n  registry: \"https://agentcenter.app\",\n  agent: \"claude\",\n};\n\nfunction ensureConfigDir() {\n  if (!existsSync(CONFIG_DIR)) mkdirSync(CONFIG_DIR, { recursive: true });\n}\n\nexport async function loadConfig(): Promise<Config> {\n  try {\n    const raw = await readFile(CONFIG_FILE, \"utf8\");\n    const parsed = parse(raw) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    const merged: Config = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...parsed };\n    if (typeof merged.registry !== \"string\") merged.registry = DEFAULT_CONFIG.registry;\n    if (typeof merged.agent !== \"string\") merged.agent = DEFAULT_CONFIG.agent;\n    return merged;\n  } catch (error: unknown) {\n    const code = (error as { code?: string })?.code;\n    // Treat missing file and malformed TOML as \"use defaults\"; rethrow everything else\n    // (permissions, IO, etc.) so the user sees the actual problem.\n    if (code === \"ENOENT\") return { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG };\n    if (error instanceof SyntaxError) return { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG };\n    // smol-toml throws TomlError on malformed input; detect by name to avoid coupling to its type.\n    if ((error as { name?: string })?.name === \"TomlError\") return { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG };\n    throw error;\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function saveConfig(config: Config): Promise<void> {\n  ensureConfigDir();\n  await writeFile(CONFIG_FILE, stringify(config as Record<string, unknown>), \"utf8\");\n}\n\nexport async function getConfigValue(key: string): Promise<unknown> {\n  const config = await loadConfig();\n  return config[key];\n}\n\nexport async function setConfigValue(key: string, value: string): Promise<void> {\n  const config = await loadConfig();\n  config[key] = value;\n  await saveConfig(config);\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, rmSync, statSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { writeFile } from \"fs/promises\";\nimport { homedir } from \"os\";\nimport { dirname, join } from \"path\";\nimport { unzipSync } from \"fflate\";\n\nconst SKILLS_DIR = join(homedir(), \".claude\", \"skills\");\n\nexport async function installSkill(slug: string, zipBuffer: ArrayBuffer): Promise<string> {\n  const destDir = join(SKILLS_DIR, slug);\n  if (!existsSync(SKILLS_DIR)) mkdirSync(SKILLS_DIR, { recursive: true });\n  if (existsSync(destDir)) rmSync(destDir, { recursive: true, force: true });\n  mkdirSync(destDir, { recursive: true });\n\n  const files = unzipSync(new Uint8Array(zipBuffer));\n  try {\n    for (const [entryPath, content] of Object.entries(files)) {\n      if (entryPath.endsWith(\"/\")) continue; // skip directory entries\n      const dest = join(destDir, entryPath);\n      const parentDir = dirname(dest);\n      if (!existsSync(parentDir)) mkdirSync(parentDir, { recursive: true });\n      await writeFile(dest, content);\n    }\n  } catch (err) {\n    // Don't leave half-written skills on disk; the next install attempt will then\n    // start from a clean slate instead of merging onto a corrupt tree.\n    rmSync(destDir, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    throw err;\n  }\n\n  return destDir;\n}\n\nexport async function uninstallSkill(slug: string): Promise<boolean> {\n  const destDir = join(SKILLS_DIR, slug);\n  if (!existsSync(destDir)) return false;\n  rmSync(destDir, { recursive: true, force: true });\n  return true;\n}\n\nexport function listInstalledSlugs(): string[] {\n  if (!existsSync(SKILLS_DIR)) return [];\n  return readdirSync(SKILLS_DIR).filter((name: string) =>\n    statSync(join(SKILLS_DIR, name)).isDirectory()\n  );\n}\n"
}

## Filter Drawer Pickers: Next.js to Vue Port Guide

### DeptPicker (Single-Select Hierarchical Tree Popover)

**UI Shape:** Popover (360px wide) with two sections:
- Header: three quick-access chips (Mine, Org, All Departments) with toggle styling
- Body: scrollable hierarchical tree of departments with expand/collapse chevrons (max-height 288px)

**Single-Select Semantics:** Clicking a department node immediately updates the filter; no submit button. Default = user's current dept (MY_DEPT_ID); selecting "All" disables the filter.

**Data Source:** Hardcoded nested `DEPARTMENTS` array from `shared/data/departments.ts` (recursive structure with id, name, nameZh, children).

**Filter Key:** `dept` (string, dotted path like `eng.cloud.infra` or the literal `__all` for unfiltered).

**Interaction Quirks:**
- Auto-expand tree nodes along path to MY_DEPT_ID on mount
- Blue dot badge next to selected dept when not in "My Dept" mode
- "MINE" label badge on the dept node that is MY_DEPT_ID
- Breadcrumb truncation in trigger button ("Parent / Child" display)
- Smooth left-padding-based tree indentation (8px + depth * 14px)

**Locale Support:** Renders name vs nameZh based on deptPath() call with locale param.

---

### TagDrawer (Multi-Select Inline Expandable Panel)

**UI Shape:** Accordion-like inline drawer (expands within page, not modal). Wrapping layout of tag pills in a flex container.

**Multi-Select + Modes:** 
- Toggle each tag on/off by clicking
- When tags selected, shows "match mode" toggle group: "ANY" (default, omitted in URL) or "ALL"
- Active count badge on the toggle button

**Data Source:** Passed as prop `tags: TagWithCount[]` from server; fetched server-side from a tags query.

**Filter Keys:** `tags` (string array, comma-joined in URL) and `tagMatch` (enum "any" | "all", omitted when "any").

**Interaction Quirks:**
- Hardcoded "show 14 tags by default, with expandable +N more" logic
- Toggle chevron animates on expand (rotates -90°)
- Tag pills show count badges (smaller font, dimmed opacity)
- When tags selected: match-mode buttons + clear button appear below tags
- "Show less" / "Show more" buttons at bottom

**Data shape:** `{ id: string, count: number }` — tag IDs are strings, counts are integral.

---

### CreatorPicker (Single-Select Popover)

**UI Shape:** Popover (280px wide), scrollable option list (max-height 288px).

**Single-Select Semantics:** 
- Option for "Any creator" (clears filter, undefined in URL)
- List of creators from facets, each showing name or email and result count
- Click to select; immediately updates filter

**Data Source:** Passed as prop `creators: CreatorFacet[]` from `listPublishedCreators()` query.

**Filter Key:** `creator` (user ID string, omitted when undefined).

**Data Shape:** 
```ts
{
  id: string           // users.id
  name?: string        // user's display name
  email: string        // fallback; always present
  count: number        // count of published extensions by this user
}
```

**Interaction Quirks:**
- Uses creatorLabel() helper: prefer name if present and non-empty, else email
- Count shown in monospace on the right (muted color)
- "No creators yet" empty state message
- Trigger button shows selected creator's label or "Any creator"

---

### PublisherPicker (Single-Select Popover)

**UI Shape:** Popover (280px wide), scrollable option list (max-height 288px) — identical layout to CreatorPicker.

**Single-Select Semantics:** 
- Option for "Any publisher" (clears filter, undefined in URL)
- List of orgs/publishers, each with count
- Click to select; immediately updates filter

**Data Source:** Passed as prop `publishers: PublisherFacet[]` from `listPublishedPublishers()` query.

**Filter Key:** `publisher` (org ID string, omitted when undefined).

**Data Shape:**
```ts
{
  id: string          // organizations.id
  name: string        // English name
  nameZh?: string     // Chinese name (optional)
  slug: string        // URL slug
  count: number       // count of published extensions by this org
}
```

**Interaction Quirks:**
- Locale-aware label: if locale === "zh" and nameZh exists, show nameZh; else name
- Same count badge styling as CreatorPicker
- Trigger button shows selected publisher's localized name or "Any publisher"

---

### Facets Query Shape (`facets.ts`)

Both creator and publisher pickers consume SQL-based facet queries that:
- **Input:** None (hardcoded filter: `where extensions.visibility = 'published'`)
- **Output:** Sorted list of facets ordered by count descending, then by secondary sort (email/name)
- **Return Type:** Array of facet objects with id, name/nameZh (orgs only), and count
- **Database:** Joins extensions with users (for creators) or organizations (for publishers); groups by user/org ID; counts matching extensions

No hierarchical structure, no search box, no lazy loading — facets are pre-fetched and passed to components as static props.

---

### i18n Keys (`filters.*` namespace)

**DeptPicker:**
- `filters.dept.all` → "All Departments"
- `filters.dept.mine` → "My Department"
- `filters.dept.org` → "My Org"
- `filters.dept.expand` → "Expand"
- `filters.dept.collapse` → "Collapse"

**TagDrawer:**
- `filters.tagsToggle` → "Tags"
- `filters.showMoreCount` → "{count} more" (parameterized)
- `filters.showLess` → "Less"
- `filters.matchModeGroupLabel` → "Tag match mode"
- `filters.tags.any` → "Any"
- `filters.tags.all` → "All"
- `filters.tags.clear` → "Clear tags"

**CreatorPicker:**
- `filters.creator.any` → "Any creator"
- `filters.creator.empty` → "No creators yet"
- `filters.creator.label` → "Creator"

**PublisherPicker:**
- `filters.publisher.any` → "Any publisher"
- `filters.publisher.empty` → "No publishers yet"
- `filters.publisher.label` → "Publisher"

**Port Notes:** Your Nuxt setup mirrors the validator structure in `shared/validators/filters.ts`, and the composable `useFilters()` already handles URL → state → URL bidirectional syncing. The dept tree, tag multi-select with mode toggle, and facet single-selects are all compatible with reka-ui Popover, Sheet, and Checkbox primitives.

## Publish Wizard Specification: 4-Step Vue/Nuxt Port

### 1. State Shape (Wizard Root)

The wizard holds **`ManifestFormValues`** plus lifecycle metadata across steps:

```typescript
// Core form state (full Zod-validated shape)
draft: ManifestFormValues = {
  slug: string,           // Written by Basics; locked after create-draft
  name: string,           // Basics
  nameZh?: string,        // Basics (optional, collapsed panel)
  version: string,        // Basics; locked after create-draft
  category: enum (4),     // Basics: "skills" | "mcp" | "slash" | "plugins"
  scope: enum (3),        // Basics: "personal" | "org" | "enterprise"
  summary: string,        // Basics; max 80 chars (lands in DB `tagline`)
  taglineZh?: string,     // Basics (optional, collapsed panel)
  
  // Bundle step
  sourceMethod: "zip",    // Bundle; currently locked to "zip" (git/cli deferred)
  
  // Listing step
  readmeMd?: string,      // Listing; max 16k
  iconColor: enum (5),    // Listing: "indigo" | "amber" | "emerald" | "rose" | "slate"
  tagIds: string[],       // Listing; max 8 tags
  deptId?: string,        // Listing (optional department ID)
  permissions: {          // Listing; toggle per-key
    network?: boolean,
    files?: boolean,
    runtime?: boolean,
    data?: boolean,
  },
}

// Wizard lifecycle (not in ManifestFormValues)
extensionId: string | null,    // Set by create-draft; stable thereafter
versionId: string | null,      // Set by create-draft; points to R2 upload & submit target
bundleUploaded: boolean,       // Set by Bundle step's attach-file call
step: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4,      // 4 = success screen
error: { msg: string; detail?: string } | null
busy: boolean                  // During async transitions
```

### 2. Step-by-Step Breakdown

#### **Step 0: Basics** (Primary metadata)
- **Fields user touches**: name, nameZh (opt), slug, version, summary, taglineZh (opt), category (4-btn grid), scope (3-choice cards)
- **Zod gates "next"**: 
  - `name` (min 2, max 80) && 
  - `slug` (min 3, max 64, regex: `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`) && 
  - `version` (regex: `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`) && 
  - `category` ∈ enum && 
  - `scope` ∈ enum && 
  - `summary` (min 1, max 80)
- **Side effects on "next"**:
  - If `!extensionId`: call `create-draft` → sets `extensionId`, `versionId`
  - If `extensionId` exists: call `update-draft` with current values
  - Lock `slug` + `version` inputs in UI (server refuses changes post-create)
  - Auto-slug: if user types in `name` field and slug hasn't been hand-edited, re-derive slug via `slugFromName()` (lowercase, replace non-alnum runs with `-`, trim edges, cap 40)
- **UI quirks**:
  - Collapsible "Chinese translations" panel (collapsed by default, expands if either `nameZh` or `taglineZh` is filled)
  - Icon grid for category (Bolt, Globe, SlashSquare, Plug; 2×2 on mobile, 1×4 on desktop)
  - Scope as 3 PubChoice cards (each w/ title + description)

---

#### **Step 1: Bundle** (Upload mechanism)
- **Fields user touches**: `sourceMethod` (tab selector; currently zip-only), file upload
- **Zod gates "next"**: `bundleUploaded === true` (form validity doesn't matter here; only file upload counts)
- **Side effects on "next"**: None — step is complete once file is attached
- **Upload pipeline**:
  1. User selects `.zip` file (validated: extension + MIME type, size ≤ 50MB)
  2. POST `/api/upload/sign` with `{ slug, version, contentType: "application/zip", size }`
     - Returns `{ uploadUrl, r2Key }`
  3. PUT file to `uploadUrl` (10-min timeout guard)
  4. Call `attach-file` server action with `{ versionId, r2Key, size, checksumSha256 }`
     - Creates files row, links to version
  5. Set `bundleUploaded = true`; show "Check" icon + filename + "Replace" button
- **UI quirks**:
  - Drag-drop + click upload on same box
  - Git & CLI tabs stubbed (disabled/"coming soon" badge on git)
  - CLI tab shows 3 copyable commands for local publish workflow
  - Show `fileName` (original upload name) after success; allow re-upload

---

#### **Step 2: Listing** (Marketplace presence)
- **Fields user touches**: `iconColor` (5-color swatch row), `tagIds` (tag input w/ suggestions), `deptId` (department picker popover), `readmeMd` (textarea), `permissions` (4 checkboxes)
- **Zod gates "next"**: 
  - `tagIds.length > 0` (at least 1 tag) && 
  - `readmeMd` (min 1 char, i.e. non-empty)
- **Side effects on "next"**: None — just validates
- **UI quirks**:
  - Icon preview: 16×16 box w/ initial letter, colored per `iconColor`, next to 5 color swatches
  - Tag input: flat field that accepts tags (Enter to add, Backspace-when-empty to remove), max 8 total
    - Shows 6 suggested tags below (from hardcoded list: "stable", "beta", "official", "ai", "search", "data", "productivity") filtered to not-yet-added
    - At limit (8 tags), input disables w/ "Limit reached" placeholder
  - Dept picker: popover button showing breadcrumb path (e.g. "Sales / Americas / US East"), flat list w/ depth-based indentation
  - README: monospace textarea, 8 rows, max 16k chars
  - Permissions: 4 toggle buttons (network, files, runtime, data), each shows as pressed/unpressed state

---

#### **Step 3: Review** (Read-only summary + submit)
- **Fields user sees**: All prior steps summarized (name-slug-version-summary-type-scope-method-bundle-tags-dept-readme-perms), none editable here
- **Zod gates "submit"**: `bundleUploaded === true` (all other fields must be valid by now)
- **Side effects on "submit"**:
  1. Call `update-draft` one final time (to persist any Listing-step edits the user made)
  2. Call `submit-for-review` with `versionId`
     - Server transitions version status: `pending` → `scanning`
     - Queues scan job via Inngest
  3. Set `step = 4` (success)
- **UI quirks**:
  - "Edit" link on each row jumps back to the relevant step (onJump callback)
  - Scope-aware info box: if `scope === "personal"`, green check + "Auto-publishes immediately"; else amber clock + "Awaits review"
  - Publisher Terms plain text (link not yet live)

---

#### **Step 4: Success Screen** (End state)
- Single-use card with checkmark, scope-aware messaging, link back to `/publish` dashboard
- Only shown after successful submit

---

### 3. Live Preview (Right Sidebar, Desktop-Only)

- **Pure derived view** — no fetching, no effects. Recalculates every render from current `draft`.
- **Mirrors these fields**:
  - Extension listing card: initial letter in `iconColor` box, `name`, `category` (localized), `summary`, first 4 tags (+ "+X more" if > 4)
  - Manifest JSON: stable serialization of
    ```json
    {
      "name": draft.slug || "your-extension",
      "displayName": draft.name || "Your Extension",
      "type": draft.category,
      "version": draft.version || "0.0.0",
      "scope": draft.scope,
      "description": draft.summary || "",
      "tags": draft.tagIds,
      "department": draft.deptId || undefined,
      "permissions": [ /* enabled keys only */ ]
    }
    ```
  - Strips empty strings and falsy permissions to avoid churn on keystroke

---

### 4. Edit/Resume Flow

**How `publish/[id]/edit/page` rehydrates:**

1. Server action `getDraft(extensionId)`:
   - Loads extension row + latest version
   - Owner-checks; returns 404 if not owner
   - Checks version status: if not `"pending"`, redirect to `/publish` (can't resume non-draft)
   - Returns `ResumeDraft` struct with `formValues` (full ManifestFormValues) + metadata
2. Passes `resume` prop to `UploadWizard`
3. Wizard initializes:
   - `step = resume.bundleUploaded ? 3 : 1` (if bundle uploaded, jump to Review; else go to Bundle)
   - `extensionId` pre-filled (no create-draft on next)
   - All form fields pre-filled from `formValues`
   - Slug + version inputs rendered as `readOnly` (visual hint, server enforces via security check)

**You'll need to add a Nuxt `get-draft.get.ts` endpoint** returning:
```typescript
{
  ok: true;
  draft: {
    extensionId: string;
    versionId: string;
    slug: string;
    version: string;
    name: string;
    category: string;
    scope: string;
    bundleUploaded: boolean;
    formValues: ManifestFormValues;
  };
} | {
  ok: false;
  error: "not_found" | "unauthenticated";
}
```

---

### 5. DiscardButton

- **Where**: Dashboard extension row (one per draft)
- **Props**: `extensionId`, `extensionName` (for confirm dialog)
- **Action**: 
  - `window.confirm("Are you sure you want to discard [name]?")`
  - If OK: POST `/api/internal/publish/discard` with `{ extensionId }`
  - Server deletes extension + cascading versions/tags/files
  - Success: `router.refresh()` (revalidate server component)
- **Constraints**: Only works on `visibility === "draft"` (server rejects else)

---

### 6. Submit Semantics

**Order of operations** (Listing → Review → Submit):

1. **Basics → Bundle transition** (`advanceFromBasics`):
   - POST `create-draft` OR PUT `update-draft` (Basics values only)
   - Sets `extensionId`, `versionId`
   - Advances to step 1 (Bundle)

2. **Bundle → Listing transition**:
   - No server call; just validate `bundleUploaded === true`
   - Advance to step 2

3. **Listing → Review transition**:
   - No server call; validate Listing fields
   - Advance to step 3

4. **Review → Submit**:
   - PUT `update-draft` with all current fields (ensures Listing edits persisted)
   - POST `submit-for-review` with `versionId`
     - Server checks bundle exists (`bundleFileId !== null`)
     - Transitions version: `pending` → `scanning`
     - Enqueues Inngest scan job
   - If either fails, surface error and stay on Review
   - On success, set `step = 4`

5. **Save Draft** (header button, any step):
   - Enabled if `extensionId` exists OR Basics is valid (can create first)
   - Calls create-draft or update-draft
   - Redirects to `/publish` (dashboard)

---

### 7. Patterns That Don't Port Cleanly

**React → Vue differences to handle:**

| React | Vue Equivalent | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `useFormState` (server action polling) | `$fetch` + `ref` + try/catch | Vue uses explicit async/await, not form transitions |
| RHF resolver chains (Zod schema to field validation) | vee-validate composable + Zod | Validate on blur/submit, not per-keystroke |
| Server components (async `getDraft` in page.tsx) | Nuxt server middleware / `defineEventHandler` | Nuxt has built-in SSR, no need for separate "server component" concept |
| `useTransition` / `startTransition` | `ref` flag + async function | Vue doesn't have automatic request deduplication; manage state explicitly |
| `readOnly` prop (UI hint) | `:disabled` or `readonly` attr | Both work; server always enforces the constraint |
| Auto-slug derivation on name change | `watch(name)` + patch | Same logic, but explicit watcher instead of render-phase side effect |
| "Step validity" array | Computed property + validation logic | Can use `computed(() => ({ basics: ..., bundle: ..., ... }))` |
| Shared error codes (KNOWN_ERROR_CODES set) | Enum or const object + i18n key lookup | Same approach, just const instead of Set |

**Key contract differences:**
- Nuxt endpoints already validate input + throw errors; no need for client-side guards before calling
- Icon colors + department flattening logic can be shared (already in Nuxt validator + data files)
- Slugify function is pure; copy to Nuxt or export from shared utils

---

### Summary Table: Zod Schemas in Use

| Step | Field(s) | Zod Rule | Locked? |
|------|---------|----------|--------|
| 0 | slug | min 3, max 64, regex | After create-draft |
| 0 | name | min 2, max 80 | No |
| 0 | version | semver regex | After create-draft |
| 0 | summary | min 1, max 80 | No |
| 0 | category | enum (4 values) | No |
| 0 | scope | enum (3 values) | No |
| 1 | (file) | .zip, ≤50MB | — |
| 2 | tagIds | array, max 8 | No |
| 2 | readmeMd | max 16k chars | No |
| 2 | iconColor | enum (5 values) | No |
| 2 | deptId | string (optional) | No |
| 2 | permissions | partial record | No |
| All | sourceMethod | literal "zip" | No (for now) |

All schemas are in `/shared/validators/manifest.ts` (already synced between codebases).

3	  searchParamsToInput,
4	  serializeFilters,
5	  type Filters,
6	} from "~~/shared/validators/filters"
7	
8	export type FilterUpdate = Partial<Filters>
9	
10	export function useFilters() {
11	  const route = useRoute()
12	  const router = useRouter()
13	  const localePath = useLocalePath()
14	
15	  const filters = computed<Filters>(() => {
16	    const params = new URLSearchParams()
17	    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(route.query)) {
18	      if (Array.isArray(v)) {
19	        for (const item of v) if (item !== null) params.append(k, String(item))
20	      } else if (v !== null && v !== undefined) {
21	        params.append(k, String(v))
22	      }
23	    }
24	    return parseFilters(searchParamsToInput(params))
25	  })
26	
27	  function update(partial: FilterUpdate) {
28	    const next: FilterUpdate = { ...filters.value, ...partial }
29	    if (!("page" in partial)) next.page = undefined
30	    const params = serializeFilters(next)
31	    const qs = params.toString()
32	    const path = route.path
33	    router.replace(qs ? `${path}?${qs}` : path)
34	  }
35	
36	  function hrefForFilters(partial: FilterUpdate, basePath = "/extensions") {
37	    const next: FilterUpdate = { ...filters.value, ...partial }
38	    if (!("page" in partial)) next.page = undefined
39	    const params = serializeFilters(next)
40	    const qs = params.toString()
41	    const path = localePath(basePath)
42	    return qs ? `${path}?${qs}` : path
43	  }
44	
45	  return { filters, update, hrefForFilters }
46	}
47
